title: Patchwork: Micro-actor library for one-click remediation and safe rollback
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Goal: Build a small, typed micro-actor ("repairlet") library that lets on-call and support engineers run safe, parameterized remediation actions from the console or via the support CLI. Repairlets are single-purpose, idempotent, tested units that implement one remediation step (eg. rotate-ssh-key, restart-pool-node, remove-stuck-job). They will be composable into runbooks-as-tasks and invoked by the existing playflow runner with clear safety gates and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Implement repairlet SDK (Python + Typescript wrappers) with typed inputs and output schema
Every repairlet must support dry-run, validate, execute, and rollback modes
Console integration: UI button to preview, run dry-run, and execute with 2-step confirmation
CLI integration: opsctl repairlet run <name> --params file.json --dry-run
Telemetry: emit start/finish/rollback events to ops-trace and link to incident ID
Safety: circuit-breaker prevents automated composition from running high-risk repairlets unless canary enabled
tasks: Design typed API for repairlet inputs/outputs (Spec + examples)
Prototype Python SDK and small TS shim for Console invocation
Implement 5 initial repairlets: rotate-ssh-key, restart-gpu-pool, flush-cache-prefix, evict-worker, promote-fallback-model
Add dry-run/validate/rollback primitives to runtime, ensure idempotency tests
Console UX: preview modal, run button, and async job link
Telemetry: hook events into ops-trace and add dashboard panels
Write runbook examples that compose repairlets for common incidents
Security review and KMS integration for secrets used by repairlets
